title: Persistent Min Stack
description:
Design an immutable, versioned **Persistent Min Stack** (`PersistentMinStack`) where every `push` and `pop` leaves all previous versions intact and produces a new sequential version ID (`1, 2, 3, ...`), all in `O(1)` time and `O(1)` extra space per operation.

Implement the `PersistentMinStack` class:
- `PersistentMinStack()` initializes version `0` as an empty stack.
- `int push(int version, int val)` creates a new version equal to `version` with `val` pushed on top, and returns the new version ID.
- `int pop(int version)` creates a new version equal to `version` with its top element removed, and returns the new version ID.
- `int top(int version)` returns the top element of `version`.
- `int getMin(int version)` returns the minimum element currently in `version`.
constraints: Every version argument is a previously created version ID (0 <= version <= latestVersion).
Methods pop, top, and getMin are always called on non-empty versions.
At most 5 * 10^4 calls will be made across all methods.
hints: Represent stack nodes as persistent tree nodes storing (val, runningMin, parentNode), with node 0 as the empty sentinel.
Keep an array nodeOfVersion mapping each version ID to its head node: push creates one new child node in O(1), and pop simply maps the new version ID to parent[nodeOfVersion[version]] in O(1).

examples.explanation: v1 = [5], v2 = [5, 2] (min 2), v3 branches from v1 to [5, 8] (min 5), v4 pops v2 back to [5] (top 5, min 5).
Popping a single-element version produces an empty version that can be pushed onto again cleanly.
Multiple branches from the same ancestor version remain completely independent.
